newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks down in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks down in thin trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended marginally lower in thin sessions with falls in banks and small gains in manufacturing.
Bogota's IBB index dipped 0.1 percent to 1,078.89 amid a 471.2 million peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 0.07 percent to 16,699.94 amid a one billion peso trade.
"The markets were very slow. There really was nothing exceptional. Foreign funds mostly stayed away," one Bogota trader said.
Banco de Bogota fell 0.78 percent to 6,300 in Bogota and 0.79 percent to the same price in Medellin. Banco Bancoquia dropped 0.44 percent to 3,365 in Bogota and 1.18 percent to 3,350 in Medellin.

Brewing giant Bavaria edged up 0.42 percent to 7,080 in Bogota and 0.43 percent to the same price in Medellin. Prices were marginally up on local, unconfirmed press reports that Bavaria had signed a deal with Argenitinian capital goods manufacturer Pescarmona, one Bogota trader said.
One of the biggest volumes was in cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, part of the powerful Sindicato Antiqueno industrial conglomerate, accounting for 637 million pesos in both markets.
